originality.rationale: Parkhomenko 2001 section 5 (full primary PDF examined) enumerates four-cube cyclic change-number types and the total 1344, but not signed inclusion-exclusion edge-character sums. Chebiryak and Kroening 2008 primary full text tabulates 1344 cycles and nine automorphism cycle classes, but no Walsh edge-support moments. Dvorak and Caha-Koubek accessible journal statements concern existence with prescribed edges, not signed three-edge counts. published research index and comparisons with previously recorded mathematical statements distinguish hypercube Hamilton cycles from cube perfect matchings and Hamilton cycles of complete graphs. The six zero frequency-orbit census and the forced/unforced boundary have no found stronger equivalent; residual unindexed priority uncertainty is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Cyclic Gray codes are the canonical Hamilton cycle ensemble in a 4-cube and have important coordinate/hypercube symmetries. Their full degree-at-most-three Walsh observation boundary is not a routine restatement of the established count of 1344: every singleton has symmetric cancellation, all 496 pairs remain nonzero, while 1056 of 1120 cubic zeros require non-star higher correlations. The exact six geometric orbits characterize the first nontrivial cancellation geometries and can serve as rigorous finite benchmarks for constrained-edge sampling and harmonic recovery. No general or global recovery theorem is claimed.
